dedupe_keys.name: a detailed damage investigation of an instrumented ductile reinforced concrete building with precast hollow core floors following the 2016 m 7 8 kaikoura earthquake

description: A Detailed Damage Investigation of an Instrumented Ductile Reinforced Concrete Building with Precast Hollow-core Floors Following the 2016 M-7.8 Kaikoura Earthquake is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "field recon", published or maintained by Mohamed Mostafa, University of Auckland (aucklanduni.ac.nz). The dataset represents one of the most complete datasets and in-depth investigations publicly available of an instrumented building subjected to a design-level earthquake. This dataset contains detailed damage data from a ductile reinforced concrete building with prestressed precast hollow-core floors. The building investigated was located in Wellington, New Zealand. Coverage: New Zealand, 15 km north-east of Culverden, North Canterbury, starting near the town of Waiau.. DesignSafe files it as a "field recon" project. Keywords: Earthquake Reconnaissance, Structural Damage, Reinforced Concrete, Precast Hollow-core Floors, Laser Scanning, Structure From Motion. Published 2023-03-20. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is ODC-By-1.0. Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
